attacks.claim: A very long unbroken URL in an expanded or leading-link description may overflow the layout on phones, because pre-line does not break long words. The PR adds no overflow-wrap rule. This is also true of the old behaviour for pasted URLs.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no overflow-wrap or word-break styling for .item-description__body links

attacks.claim: TRAILING_PUNCT strips a closing ')' unconditionally, so URLs that legitimately end in ')' (e.g. Wikipedia-style paths) are linked incorrectly. This is a cosmetic edge case.
No security issue found. Text is rendered as React children, only http(s) URLs become hrefs, and the link has rel=noopener noreferrer nofollow. The tests cover javascript: URLs and injected markup.
attacks.evidence: rel="noopener noreferrer nofollow"; test asserts no and only the http link
